1.explanation: Both the React and vanilla-JS implementations include code specifically to render and toggle a dropdown variant of the tabs. In the React version, the Tabs class defines state.dropdownHidden, derives state from props, and implements handleDropdownClick plus conditional JSX in render() to show a select-style menu. In the vanilla JS version, the Tab class implements _updateMenuState, _handleDocumentClick, _handleKeyDown (to open/close the menu), and _updateTriggerText to manage the trigger button’s label. To remove the dropdown variant, these classes and methods must be updated or removed.
1.bug_scenario: The first screenshot shows the Tabs component collapsed into a native HTML <select> dropdown when the available width narrows. The second shows the full horizontal tab list in wide view. This automatic switch to a dropdown is confusing for screen‐reader users (it changes the markup to a listbox) and doesn’t respond to the actual component width, only the viewport width—both of which the proposal aims to remove.

2.explanation: The React Tabs class (in packages/react) contains all of the state and logic responsible for hiding/showing the dropdown trigger (dropdownHidden state), rendering the <select>-style trigger in render(), and toggling it in handleDropdownClick. Similarly, the vanilla JS Tab class (in packages/components) drives the narrow-mode dropdown via its internal _updateMenuState method and keeps the trigger text in sync via _updateTriggerText. Removing or disabling these methods and the related JSX/css in render() will eliminate the dropdown variant across both implementations.
2.bug_scenario: On narrow viewports the Tabs component silently switches from a horizontal tablist into a native <select>-style dropdown. The first screenshot shows the dropdown variant (“Tab label 2” selected, arrow icon), and the second shows the normal horizontal tabs. The proposal is to remove this automatic dropdown variant entirely and always render the standard tablist.
